correctness.rationale: PASS: Used Euler identity in characteristic 3 and all-nonzero supports of a principal submatrix of B=[[a,-d,-e],[-d,b,-f],[-e,-f,c]] to reconstruct the exact geometric singularity criterion. All a,b,c must be nonzero and at most one mixed coefficient can be nonzero, joining opposite signs. This gives 8 diagonal plus 24 one-mixed vectors, or 16 modulo nonzero scalar. The invertible (U+V,U-V,W) quartic identity and permutations collapse the 16 to three projective types. For the three signed-coordinate involutions, genus-one quotients and a genus-zero common quotient split H^1; rational counts of elliptic quotients (4,4,4), (2,4,4) or (6,4,4) yield exactly the three stated Weil polynomials and 3-ranks. A fresh independent exhaustive algebraic support computation covered all 728 nonzero coefficient vectors and a separate point count over F3 verified (4:8,2:12,6:12) at vector level. This point count alone does not prove geometric smoothness or all Weil factors; the linear-algebra criterion and quotient argument do.

final_claim: Among projective-scalar normalized sextuples over F3 in the split Ciani quartic linear system, exactly 16 are geometrically smooth; their curves form three PGL3(F3) classes of multiplicities 4,6,6, with point counts 4,2,6 and Weil numerators (1+3T^2)^3 and (1±2T+3T^2)(1+3T^2)^2, giving 3-ranks 0,1,1.
